verses.pali: “Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, yāni kānici tantāvutānaṁ vatthānaṁ, kesakambalo tesaṁ paṭikiṭṭho akkhāyati.
verses.english: “Mendicants, a hair blanket is said to be the worst kind of woven cloth.

verses.pali: Kesakambalo, bhikkhave, sīte sīto, uṇhe uṇho, dubbaṇṇo, duggandho, dukkhasamphasso.
verses.english: It’s cold in the cold, hot in the heat, ugly, smelly, and unpleasant to touch.

verses.pali: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, yāni kānici puthusamaṇabrāhmaṇavādānaṁ makkhalivādo tesaṁ paṭikiṭṭho akkhāyati.
verses.english: In the same way, the teaching of the bamboo-staffed ascetic is said to be the worst of all the doctrines of the various ascetics and brahmins.
The bamboo-staffed ascetic, that futile man, has this doctrine and view:
‘There is no power in deeds, action, or energy.’

verses.pali: Yepi te, bhikkhave, ahesuṁ atītamaddhānaṁ arahanto sammāsambuddhā, tepi bhagavanto kammavādā ceva ahesuṁ kiriyavādā ca vīriyavādā ca.
verses.english: Those who were perfected ones, fully awakened Buddhas in the past also taught the efficacy of deeds, action, and energy.
But the bamboo-staffed ascetic opposes them by saying:
‘There is no power in deeds, action, or energy.’

verses.pali: Yepi te, bhikkhave, bhavissanti anāgatamaddhānaṁ arahanto sammāsambuddhā, tepi bhagavanto kammavādā ceva bhavissanti kiriyavādā ca vīriyavādā ca.
verses.english: Those who will be perfected ones, fully awakened Buddhas in the future will also teach the efficacy of deeds, action, and energy.
But the bamboo-staffed ascetic opposes them by saying:
‘There is no power in deeds, action, or energy.’

verses.pali: Ahampi, bhikkhave, etarahi arahaṁ sammāsambuddho kammavādo ceva kiriyavādo ca vīriyavādo ca.
verses.english: I too, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha in the present, teach the efficacy of deeds, action, and energy.
But the bamboo-staffed ascetic opposes me by saying:
‘There is no power in deeds, action, or energy.’

verses.pali: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, nadīmukhe khippaṁ uḍḍeyya bahūnaṁ macchānaṁ ahitāya dukkhāya anayāya byasanāya;
verses.english: It’s like a trap set at the mouth of a river, which would bring harm, suffering, calamity, and disaster for many fish.

verses.pali: evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, makkhali moghapuriso manussakhippaṁ maññe loke uppanno bahūnaṁ sattānaṁ ahitāya dukkhāya anayāya byasanāyā”ti.
verses.english: In the same way that futile man the bamboo-staffed ascetic is a trap for humans, it seems to me. He has come into the world for the harm, suffering, calamity, and disaster of many beings.”
